raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The frontal and lateral chest X-rays demonstrate a large anterior mediastinal mass that obscures the hilar vessels (positive hilum-overlay sign), confirming its anterior location. The presence of bilateral basal opacities with meniscus signs indicates pleural effusions, which, in the context of an aggressive anterior mediastinal mass, is highly suggestive of thymic carcinoma with pleural metastases.
